subject: Product compatibility checklist and telemetry contract for AstraGrid launch
messages:
From: Emily Park <emily@astragrid.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Cc: partners@astragrid.com
Date: Thu, 14 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Product compatibility checklist and telemetry contract for AstraGrid launch

Hi Vivek / Laura —

Thanks for the quick intros last week. AstraGrid is planning to list a managed connector that uses Redwood inference for code-assist features in our marketplace. Before we lock the listing date we need to align on two things that affect our go/no-go:

1) Compatibility checklist — minimal runtime & entitlement requirements we can show on our listing (model variants supported, tokenization expectations, packaging notes for ISV integrations). I attached a draft checklist (astragrid-compatibility-checklist.pdf) with questions on header parsing and recommended timeouts.

2) Telemetry contract — we need a lightweight telemetry spec so we can show usage numbers in our partner dashboard and meet our analytics SLAs without exposing PII. Attached is our suggested schema (astragrid-telemetry-schema.csv). We need to confirm the exact fields you can emit and the latency guarantees for metrics ingestion.

High-level asks from our side:
- Can Redwood commit to the checklist items within two sprints?
- Can you surface a contact who owns telemetry ingestion for partner integrations?
- Any known blockers for packaging the connector as a single artifact (we support zip/OCI images)

We can be flexible on the exact timing, but target launch is mid-November — would like to lock decisions by Oct 28. I attached the drafts for your review.

Would you be available for a 30-minute alignment call next week (Oct 18/19)?

Thanks,
Emily Park
Head of Partnerships, AstraGrid
emily@astragrid.com

Attachments: astragrid-compatibility-checklist.pdf, astragrid-telemetry-schema.csv

Subject: Re: Product compatibility checklist and telemetry contract for AstraGrid launch

Emily — thanks for the clear write-up and the attachments. I've skimmed the checklist and telemetry schema; high level yes — we can support this but want to call out a couple of implementation notes so expectations are aligned. Looping in Laura (product), Ben (solutions) and Karthik (integrations) to own details.

Quick answers up front:
- Commitment window: we can aim to complete the checklist sign-off within two sprints (target Oct 28) if there are no major SDK surface changes.
- Telemetry contact: Ben will take point on telemetry ingestion fields and will confirm what we can expose without touching PII/compliance boundaries.
- Packaging: Redwood supports zip and OCI-style bundles; there is a known quirk with older connector manifests that expect a static model path. If AstraGrid can provide a sample package we can validate quickly.

Proposed two-step plan:
1) Tactical: sign checklist + sample package validation (2 weeks).
2) Pilot: telemetry ingestion contract + dashboard wiring (follow-on sprint) — this includes an opt-in flag for partners.

Ben / Karthik — can you take the checklist and telemetry CSV, add any required fields, and return an integration playbook doc? I've created a placeholder (Redwood-integration-ops.md) which I'll attach to this thread.

Emily — are you free Oct 19 at 10:00am PT for a short sync? If that doesn't work we'll propose alternatives.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.ai

Attachments referenced: Redwood-integration-ops.md

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Emily Park <emily@astragrid.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 Oct 2026 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Product compatibility checklist and telemetry contract for AstraGrid launch

Emily / team — I've reviewed the checklist and the telemetry CSV. A few technical notes from runtime side:

- Tokenization: we support byte-level and sentencepiece tokenizers; ensure your connector declares which tokenizer to use. If you rely on model-specific token offsets we should capture that in the manifest.

- Model routing: Redwood routes requests to model variants based on tenant routing rules. If AstraGrid wants to pin to a single variant for performance guarantees we need an explicit entitlement field in the manifest (we can add entitlement: "pin_model_variant").

- Backwards compatibility: older ISV packages sometimes embed a hardcoded model path. We can handle this by adding a compatibility shim but that is an exception and requires a short-lived feature flag.

I've created a Jira ticket to track the shim and entitlement flag: SUP-8921 (https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/SUP-8921). Will add acceptance criteria and a test plan there.

Telemetry specifics:
- We can emit non-PII usage metrics (consumer counts, request latencies, token consumption buckets) to an event stream that AstraGrid can consume. We won't emit user prompt text.
- Event ingestion latency: typical <10s to partner dashboard when streamed; bulk batch export is available nightly (T+1).

I'll draft the first pass of the integration playbook (will post link to the doc in this thread).

—Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai

Emily / Vivek — quick operational ask from the integrations team.

On Thu, Oct 14, 2026 at 09:12 AM Emily Park <emily@astragrid.com> wrote:
> Hi Vivek / Laura —
> 
> Thanks for the quick intros last week. AstraGrid is planning to list a managed connector that uses Redwood inference for code-assist features in our marketplace. Before we lock the listing date we need to align on two things that affect our go/no-go:

We can support the plan and the timelines, but to avoid scope creep we will need either:
- a short-term exception to our packaging policy for legacy manifests (we can enable the compatibility shim under feature flag SUP-8921), OR
- AstraGrid provides a sample connector package (zip or OCI) that we can validate against our CI.

If AstraGrid can provide the sample package by Oct 20 we can validate it in our CI and return a pass/fail and a minimal remediation list by Oct 26. Otherwise the packaging exception work (feature-flag shim + testing) will add ~2 additional weeks to the timeline.

Resource ask: I will need 1 engineer (2 days) and a QA pass (1 day) the week of Oct 26 to validate and finalize the checklist. Please confirm if AstraGrid can drop the sample package to a shared link.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Integrations — Redwood Inference
